Our Milky Way has a supermassive black hole at its center, but our galaxy is not unusual. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has provided astronomers with many observations of galaxies with black holes at their centers. Astronomers have connected the evolution of these black holes to their galaxies, a process called co-evolution. 

Further, through observations of the early universe, Webb has discovered a new class of objects known as little red dots, named for their compact, red appearance. These objects tend to appear even in observations where they weren’t the focus and astronomers note that nothing we’ve seen before looks like them.

In this video, dive deeper into the potential origins of black holes, theories on how they develop, and how they grow with galaxies.
